7018.text: She spoke to him according to these words, saying, "The Hebrew servant, whom you have brought to us, came in to me to mock me,

7019.text: and it happened, as I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment by me, and ran outside."

7020.text: It happened, when his master heard the words of his wife, which she spoke to him, saying, "This is what your servant did to me," that his wrath was kindled.

7021.text: Joseph's master took him, and put him into the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were bound, and he was there in custody.

7022.text: But the Lord was with Joseph, and showed kindness to him, and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.

7023.text: The keeper of the prison committed to Joseph's hand all the prisoners who were in the prison. Whatever they did there, he was responsible for it.

7024.text: The keeper of the prison did not look after anything that was under his hand, because the Lord was with him; and that which he did, the Lord made it prosper.

7025.text: It happened after these things, that the butler of the king of Egypt and his baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt.

7026.text: Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.

7027.text: He put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place where Joseph was bound.

7028.text: The captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph, and he took care of them. They stayed in prison many days.

7029.text: They both dreamed a dream, each man his dream, in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were bound in the prison.

7030.text: Joseph came in to them in the morning, and saw them, and saw that they were sad.

7031.text: He asked Pharaoh's officers who were with him in custody in his master's house, saying, "Why do you look so sad today?"

7032.text: They said to him, "We have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it." Joseph said to them, "Do not interpretations belong to God? Please tell it to me."

7033.text: The chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, "In my dream, behold, a vine was in front of me,

7034.text: and in the vine were three branches. It was as though it budded, its blossoms shot forth, and its clusters brought forth ripe grapes.

7035.text: Pharaoh's cup was in my hand; and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh's cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand."

7036.text: Joseph said to him, "This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days.

7037.text: Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up your head, and restore you to your office. You will give Pharaoh's cup into his hand, the way you did when you were his cupbearer.

7038.text: But remember me when it will be well with you, and show kindness, please, to me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.

7039.text: For indeed, I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews, and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon."

7040.text: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said to Joseph, "I also was in my dream, and behold, three baskets of white bread were on my head.

7041.text: In the uppermost basket there was all kinds of baked food for Pharaoh, and the birds ate them out of the basket on my head."

7042.text: Joseph answered, "This is its interpretation. The three baskets are three days.

7043.text: Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up your head from off you, and will hang you on a tree; and the birds will eat your flesh from off you."

7044.text: It happened the third day, which was Pharaoh's birthday, that he made a feast for all his servants, and he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker among his servants.

7045.text: He restored the chief cupbearer to his position again, and he gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand;

7046.text: but he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph had interpreted to them.

7047.text: Yet the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.

7048.text: It happened at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and behold, he stood by the river.

7049.text: Behold, there came up out of the river seven cattle, sleek and fat, and they fed in the marsh grass.

7050.text: Behold, seven other cattle came up after them out of the river, ugly and thin, and stood by the other cattle on the brink of the river.

7051.text: The ugly and thin cattle ate up the seven sleek and fat cattle. So Pharaoh awoke.

7052.text: He slept and dreamed a second time: and behold, seven heads of grain came up on one stalk, healthy and good.

7053.text: Behold, seven heads of grain, thin and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them.

7054.text: The thin heads of grain blasted with the east wind swallowed up the seven healthy and full ears. Pharaoh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.

7055.text: It happened in the morning that his spirit was troubled, and he sent and called for all of Egypt's magicians and wise men. Pharaoh told them his dreams, but there was no one who could interpret them to Pharaoh.

7056.text: Then the chief cupbearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, "I remember my faults today.

7057.text: Pharaoh was angry with his servants, and put me in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, me and the chief baker.

7058.text: We dreamed a dream in one night, I and he. We dreamed each man according to the interpretation of his dream.

7059.text: There was with us there a young man, a Hebrew, servant to the captain of the guard, and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams. To each man according to his dream he interpreted.

7060.text: It happened, as he interpreted to us, so it was: he restored me to my office, and he hanged him."

7061.text: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon. He shaved himself, changed his clothing, and came in to Pharaoh.

7062.text: Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it. I have heard it said of you, that when you hear a dream you can interpret it."

7063.text: Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, "Without God an answer of welfare shall not be given to Pharaoh."

7064.text: Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, "In my dream, behold, I stood on the brink of the river:

7065.text: and behold, there came up out of the river seven cattle, fat and sleek. They fed in the marsh grass,

7066.text: and behold, seven other cattle came up after them, poor and very ugly and thin, such as I never saw in all the land of Egypt for ugliness.

7067.text: The thin and ugly cattle ate up the first seven fat cattle,

7068.text: and when they had eaten them up, it couldn't be known that they had eaten them, but they were still ugly, as at the beginning. So I awoke.

7069.text: I saw in my dream, and behold, seven heads of grain came up on one stalk, full and good:

7070.text: and behold, seven heads of grain, withered, thin, and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them.

7071.text: The seven thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven good heads of grain. I told it to the magicians, but there was no one who could explain it to me."

7072.text: Joseph said to Pharaoh, "The dream of Pharaoh is one. What God is about to do he has declared to Pharaoh.

7073.text: The seven good cattle are seven years; and the seven good heads of grain are seven years. The dream is one.

7074.text: The seven thin and ugly cattle that came up after them are seven years, and also the seven empty heads of grain blasted with the east wind; they will be seven years of famine.

7075.text: That is the thing which I spoke to Pharaoh. What God is about to do he has shown to Pharaoh.

7076.text: Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt.

7077.text: There will arise after them seven years of famine, and all the plenty will be forgotten in the land of Egypt. The famine will consume the land,

7078.text: and the plenty will not be known in the land by reason of that famine which follows; for it will be very grievous.

7079.text: The dream was doubled to Pharaoh, because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.

7080.text: "Now therefore let Pharaoh look for a discreet and wise man, and set him over the land of Egypt.

7081.text: Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint overseers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt's produce in the seven plenteous years.

7082.text: Let them gather all the food of these good years that come, and lay up grain under the hand of Pharaoh for food in the cities, and let them keep it.

7083.text: The food will be for a store to the land against the seven years of famine, which will be in the land of Egypt; that the land not perish through the famine."

7084.text: The thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.

7085.text: Pharaoh said to his servants, "Can we find such a one as this, a man in whom is the Spirit of God?"

7086.text: Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Because God has shown you all of this, there is none so discreet and wise as you.

7087.text: You shall be over my house, and according to your word will all my people be ruled. Only in the throne I will be greater than you."

7088.text: Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Behold, I have set you over all the land of Egypt."

7089.text: Pharaoh took off his signet ring from his hand, and put it on Joseph's hand, and arrayed him in robes of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck,

7090.text: and he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had. They cried before him, "Bow the knee!" He set him over all the land of Egypt.

7091.text: Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I am Pharaoh, and without you shall no man lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt."

7092.text: Pharaoh called Joseph's name Zaphenath-Paneah; and he gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On as a wife. Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.

7093.text: Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Egypt.

7094.text: In the seven plenteous years the earth brought forth abundantly.

7095.text: He gathered up all the food of the seven years which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities: the food of the field, which was around every city, he laid up in the same.

7096.text: Joseph laid up grain as the sand of the sea, very much, until he stopped counting, for it was without number.

7097.text: To Joseph were born two sons before the year of famine came, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On, bore to him.

7098.text: Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, "For," he said, "God has made me forget all my toil, and all my father's house."

7099.text: The name of the second, he called Ephraim: "For God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction."

7100.text: The seven years of plenty, that were in the land of Egypt, came to an end.

7101.text: The seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph had said. There was famine in all lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.

7102.text: When all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread, and Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, "Go to Joseph. What he says to you, do."

7103.text: The famine was over all the surface of the earth. Joseph opened all the store houses, and sold to the Egyptians. The famine was severe in the land of Egypt.

7104.text: All countries came into Egypt, to Joseph, to buy grain, because the famine was severe in all the earth.

7105.text: Now Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob said to his sons, "Why do you look at one another?"

7106.text: He said, "Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there, and buy for us from there, so that we may live, and not die."

7107.text: Joseph's ten brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.

7108.text: But Jacob did not send Benjamin, Joseph's brother, with his brothers; for he said, "Lest perhaps harm happen to him."

7109.text: The sons of Israel came to buy among those who came, for the famine was in the land of Canaan.

7110.text: Joseph was the governor over the land. It was he who sold to all the people of the land. Joseph's brothers came, and bowed themselves down to him with their faces to the earth.

7111.text: Joseph saw his brothers, and he recognized them, but acted like a stranger to them, and spoke roughly with them. He said to them, "Where did you come from?" They said, "From the land of Canaan to buy food."

7112.text: Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him.

7113.text: Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed about them, and said to them, "You are spies! You have come to see the nakedness of the land."

7114.text: They said to him, "No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.

7115.text: We are all one man's sons; we are honest men. Your servants are not spies."

7116.text: He said to them, "No, but you have come to see the nakedness of the land."

7117.text: They said, "We, your servants, are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest is this day with our father, and one is no more."

7118.text: Joseph said to them, "It is like I told you, saying, 'You are spies.'

7119.text: By this you shall be tested. By the life of Pharaoh, you shall not go forth from here, unless your youngest brother comes here.

7120.text: Send one of you, and let him get your brother, and you shall be bound, that your words may be tested, whether there is truth in you, or else by the life of Pharaoh surely you are spies."

7121.text: He put them all together into custody for three days.

7122.text: Joseph said to them the third day, "Do this, and live, for I fear God.

7123.text: If you are honest men, then let one of your brothers be bound in your prison; but you go, carry grain for the famine of your houses.

7124.text: Bring your youngest brother to me; so will your words be verified, and you won't die." They did so.

7125.text: They said one to another, "We are certainly guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the distress of his soul, when he begged us, and we wouldn't listen. Therefore this distress has come upon us."

7126.text: Reuben answered them, saying, "Did I not tell you, saying, 'Do not sin against the child,' and you wouldn't listen? Therefore also, behold, his blood is required."

7127.text: They did not know that Joseph understood them; for there was an interpreter between them.

7128.text: He turned himself away from them, and wept. Then he returned to them, and spoke to them, and took Simeon from among them, and bound him before their eyes.

7129.text: Then Joseph gave a command to fill their bags with grain, and to restore every man's money into his sack, and to give them food for the way. So it was done to them.

7130.text: They loaded their donkeys with their grain, and departed from there.

7131.text: As one of them opened his sack to give his donkey food in the lodging place, he saw his money. Behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.

7132.text: He said to his brothers, "My money is restored! Behold, it is in my sack!" Their hearts failed them, and they turned trembling one to another, saying, "What is this that God has done to us?"

7133.text: They came to Jacob their father, to the land of Canaan, and told him all that had happened to them, saying,

7134.text: "The man, the lord of the land, spoke roughly with us, and took us for spies of the country.

7135.text: We said to him, 'We are honest men. We are no spies.

7136.text: We are twelve brothers, sons of our father; one is no more, and the youngest is this day with our father in the land of Canaan.'

7137.text: The man, the lord of the land, said to us, 'By this I will know that you are honest men: leave one of your brothers with me, and take grain for the famine of your houses, and go your way.

7138.text: Bring your youngest brother to me. Then I will know that you are not spies, but that you are honest men. So I will deliver your brother to you, and you shall trade in the land.'"

7139.text: It happened as they emptied their sacks, that behold, every man's bundle of money was in his sack. When they and their father saw their bundles of money, they were afraid.

7140.text: Jacob, their father, said to them, "You have bereaved me of my children! Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and you want to take Benjamin away. All these things are against me."

7141.text: Reuben spoke to his father, saying, "Kill my two sons, if I do not bring him to you. Entrust him to my care, and I will bring him to you again."

7142.text: He said, "My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he only is left. If harm happens to him along the way in which you go, then you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol."

7143.text: The famine was severe in the land.

7144.text: It happened, when they had eaten up the grain which they had brought out of Egypt, their father said to them, "Go again, buy us a little more food."

7145.text: Judah spoke to him, saying, "The man solemnly warned us, saying, 'You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.'

7146.text: If you'll send our brother with us, we'll go down and buy you food,

7147.text: but if you'll not send him, we'll not go down, for the man said to us, 'You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.'"

7148.text: Israel said, "Why did you treat me so badly, telling the man that you had another brother?"

7149.text: They said, "The man asked directly concerning ourselves, and concerning our relatives, saying, 'Is your father still alive? Have you another brother?' We just answered his questions. Is there any way we could know that he would say, 'Bring your brother down?'"

7150.text: Judah said to Israel, his father, "Send the boy with me, and we'll get up and go, so that we may live, and not die, both we, and you, and also our little ones.

7151.text: I'll be collateral for him. From my hand will you require him. If I do not bring him to you, and set him before you, then let me bear the blame forever,

7152.text: for if we hadn't delayed, surely we would have returned a second time by now."

7153.text: Their father, Israel, said to them, "If it must be so, then do this. Take from the choice fruits of the land in your bags, and carry down a present for the man, a little balm, a little honey, spices and myrrh, nuts, and almonds;

7154.text: and take double money in your hand, and take back the money that was returned in the mouth of your sacks. Perhaps it was an oversight.

7155.text: Take your brother also, get up, and return to the man.

7156.text: May God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may release to you your other brother and Benjamin. If I am bereaved of my children, I am bereaved."

7157.text: The men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and got up, went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.

7158.text: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, "Bring the men into the house, and butcher an animal, and make ready; for the men will dine with me at noon."

7159.text: The man did as Joseph commanded, and the man brought the men to Joseph's house.

7160.text: The men were afraid, because they were brought to Joseph's house; and they said, "Because of the money that was returned in our sacks at the first time, we're brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, attack us, and seize us as slaves, along with our donkeys."

7161.text: They came near to the steward of Joseph's house, and they spoke to him at the door of the house,

7162.text: and said, "Oh, my lord, we indeed came down the first time to buy food.

7163.text: When we came to the lodging place, we opened our sacks, and behold, every man's money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight. We have brought it back in our hand.

7164.text: We have brought down other money in our hand to buy food. We do not know who put our money in our sacks."

7165.text: He said, "Peace be to you. Do not be afraid. Your God, and the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks. I received your money." He brought Simeon out to them.

7166.text: The man brought the men into Joseph's house, and gave them water, and they washed their feet. He gave their donkeys fodder.

7167.text: They made ready the present for Joseph's coming at noon, for they heard that they should eat bread there.

7168.text: When Joseph came home, they brought him the present which was in their hand into the house, and bowed themselves down to him to the earth.

7169.text: He asked them of their welfare, and said, "Is your father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he yet alive?"

7170.text: They said, "Your servant, our father, is well. He is still alive." They bowed the head, and did homage.

7171.text: He lifted up his eyes, and saw Benjamin, his brother, his mother's son, and said, "Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?" He said, "God be gracious to you, my son."

7172.text: Joseph hurried, for his heart yearned over his brother; and he sought a place to weep. He entered into his room, and wept there.

7173.text: He washed his face, and came out. He controlled himself, and said, "Serve the meal."

7174.text: They served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians, that ate with him, by themselves, because the Egyptians do not eat bread with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination to the Egyptians.

7175.text: They sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth, and the men marveled one with another.

7176.text: He sent portions to them from before him, but Benjamin's portion was five times as much as any of theirs. They drank, and were merry with him.

7177.text: He commanded the steward of his house, saying, "Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put every man's money in his sack's mouth.

7178.text: Put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack's mouth of the youngest, with his grain money." He did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.

7179.text: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.

7180.text: When they had gone out of the city, and were not yet far off, Joseph said to his steward, "Up, follow after the men. When you overtake them, ask them, 'Why have you rewarded evil for good?

7181.text: Isn't this that from which my lord drinks, and by which he indeed divines? You have done evil in so doing.'"

7182.text: He overtook them, and he spoke these words to them.

7183.text: They said to him, "Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from your servants that they should do such a thing!

7184.text: Behold, the money, which we found in our sacks' mouths, we brought again to you out of the land of Canaan. How then should we steal silver or gold out of your lord's house?

7185.text: With whoever of your servants it be found, let him die, and we also will be my lord's bondservants."

7186.text: He said, "Now also let it be according to your words: he with whom it is found will be my bondservant; and you will be blameless."

7187.text: Then they hurried, and every man took his sack down to the ground, and every man opened his sack.

7188.text: He searched, beginning with the eldest, and ending at the youngest. The cup was found in Benjamin's sack.

7189.text: Then they tore their clothes, and every man loaded his donkey, and returned to the city.

7190.text: Judah and his brothers came to Joseph's house, and he was still there. They fell on the ground before him.

7191.text: Joseph said to them, "What deed is this that you have done? Do you not know that such a man as I can indeed divine?"

7192.text: Judah said, "What will we tell my lord? What will we speak? Or how will we clear ourselves? God has found out the iniquity of your servants. Behold, we are my lord's bondservants, both we, and he also in whose hand the cup is found."

7193.text: He said, "Far be it from me that I should do so. The man in whose hand the cup is found, he will be my bondservant; but as for you, go up in peace to your father."

7194.text: Then Judah came near to him, and said, "Oh, my lord, please let your servant speak a word in my lord's ears, and do not let your anger burn against your servant; for you are even as Pharaoh.

7195.text: My lord asked his servants, saying, 'Have you a father, or a brother?'

7196.text: We said to my lord, 'We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother; and his father loves him.'

7197.text: You said to your servants, 'Bring him down to me, that I may set my eyes on him.'

7198.text: We said to my lord, 'The boy can't leave his father: for if he should leave his father, his father would die.'

7199.text: You said to your servants, 'Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you will see my face no more.'

7200.text: It happened when we came up to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.

7201.text: Our father said, 'Go again, buy us a little food.'

7202.text: We said, 'We can't go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down: for we may not see the man's face, unless our youngest brother is with us.'

7203.text: Your servant, my father, said to us, 'You know that my wife bore me two sons:

7204.text: and the one went out from me, and I said, "Surely he is torn in pieces;" and I haven't seen him since.

7205.text: If you take this one also from me, and harm happens to him, you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.'

7206.text: Now therefore when I come to your servant my father, and the boy is not with us; seeing that his life is bound up in the boy's life;

7207.text: it will happen, when he sees that the boy is no more, that he will die. Your servants will bring down the gray hairs of your servant, our father, with sorrow to Sheol.

7208.text: For your servant became collateral for the boy to my father, saying, 'If I do not bring him to you, then I will bear the blame to my father forever.'

7209.text: Now therefore, please let your servant stay instead of the boy, a bondservant to my lord; and let the boy go up with his brothers.

7210.text: For how will I go up to my father, if the boy isn't with me?-lest I see the evil that will come on my father."

7211.text: Then Joseph couldn't control himself before all those who stood before him, and he cried, "Cause every man to go out from me!" No one else stood with him, while Joseph made himself known to his brothers.

7212.text: He wept aloud. The Egyptians heard, and the house of Pharaoh heard.

7213.text: Joseph said to his brothers, "I am Joseph! Does my father still live?" His brothers couldn't answer him; for they were terrified at his presence.

7214.text: Joseph said to his brothers, "Come near to me, please." They came near. "He said, I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.

7215.text: Now do not be grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.

7216.text: For these two years the famine has been in the land, and there are yet five years, in which there will be neither plowing nor harvest.

7217.text: God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant in the earth, and to save you alive by a great deliverance.

7218.text: So now it wasn't you who sent me here, but God, and he has made me a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.

7219.text: Hurry, and go up to my father, and tell him, 'This is what your son Joseph says, "God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me. Do not wait.

7220.text: You shall dwell in the land of Goshen, and you will be near to me, you, your children, your children's children, your flocks, your herds, and all that you have.

7221.text: There I will nourish you; for there are yet five years of famine; lest you come to poverty, you, and your household, and all that you have."'

7222.text: Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks to you.

7223.text: You shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that you have seen. You shall hurry and bring my father down here."

7224.text: He fell on his brother Benjamin's neck, and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.

7225.text: He kissed all his brothers, and wept on them. After that his brothers talked with him.

7226.text: The report of it was heard in Pharaoh's house, saying, "Joseph's brothers have come." It pleased Pharaoh well, and his servants.

7227.text: Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Tell your brothers, 'Do this. Load your animals, and go, travel to the land of Canaan.

7228.text: Take your father and your households, and come to me, and I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and you will eat the fat of the land.'

7229.text: Now you are commanded: do this. Take wagons out of the land of Egypt for your little ones, and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.

7230.text: Also, do not concern yourselves about your belongings, for the good of all of the land of Egypt is yours."

7231.text: The sons of Israel did so. Joseph gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the way.

7232.text: He gave each one of them changes of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.

7233.text: To his father, he sent after this manner: ten donkeys loaded with the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and provision for his father by the way.

7234.text: So he sent his brothers away, and they departed. He said to them, "See that you do not quarrel on the way."

7235.text: They went up out of Egypt, and came into the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father.

7236.text: They told him, saying, "Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt." His heart fainted, for he did not believe them.

7237.text: They told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said to them. When he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob, their father, revived.

7238.text: Israel said, "It is enough. Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die."

7239.text: Israel traveled with all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father, Isaac.

7240.text: God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night, and said, "Jacob, Jacob!" He said, "Here I am."

7241.text: He said, "I am God, the God of your father. Do not be afraid to go down into Egypt, for there I will make of you a great nation.

7242.text: I will go down with you into Egypt. I will also surely bring you up again. Joseph will close your eyes."

7243.text: Jacob rose up from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel carried Jacob, their father, their little ones, and their wives, in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent to carry him.

7244.text: They took their livestock, and their goods, which they had gotten in the land of Canaan, and came into Egypt-Jacob, and all his seed with him,

7245.text: his sons, and his sons' sons with him, his daughters, and his sons' daughters, and he brought all his seed with him into Egypt.

7246.text: These are the names of the children of Israel, who came into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Reuben, Jacob's firstborn.

7247.text: The sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.

7248.text: The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman.

7249.text: The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

7250.text: The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah; but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.

7251.text: The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puvah, Iob, and Shimron.

7252.text: The sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.

7253.text: These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan Aram, with his daughter Dinah. All the souls of his sons and his daughters were thirty-three.

7254.text: The sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.

7255.text: The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and Serah their sister. The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.

7256.text: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob, even sixteen souls.

7257.text: The sons of Rachel, Jacob's wife: Joseph and Benjamin.

7258.text: To Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him. And there were sons born to Manasseh, which the Aramean concubine bore to him: Machir. And Machir begot Gilead. And the sons of Ephraim, the brother of Manasseh: Shuthelah and Tahan. And the sons of Shuthelah: Eran

7259.text: And the sons of Benjamin: Bela, and Becher, and Ashbel. And the sons of Bela were: Gera and Naaman, and Ehi, and Rosh, and Muppim, and Huppim. And Gera begot Ard.

7260.text: These are the sons of Rachel, who were born to Jacob: all the souls were eighteen.

7262.text: The sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.

7263.text: These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob: all the souls were seven.

7264.text: All the souls who came with Jacob into Egypt, who were his direct descendants, besides Jacob's sons' wives, all the souls were sixty-six.

7265.text: The sons of Joseph, who were born to him in Egypt, were nine souls. All the souls of the house of Jacob, who came into Egypt, were seventy-five.

7266.text: He sent Judah before him to Joseph, to show the way before him to Goshen, and they came into the land of Goshen.

7267.text: Joseph made ready his chariot, and went up to meet Israel, his father, in Goshen. He presented himself to him, and fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.

7268.text: Israel said to Joseph, "Now let me die, since I have seen your face, that you are still alive."

7269.text: Joseph said to his brothers, and to his father's house, "I will go up, and speak with Pharaoh, and will tell him, 'My brothers, and my father's house, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.

7270.text: These men are shepherds, for they have been keepers of livestock, and they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have.'

7271.text: It will happen, when Pharaoh summons you, and will say, 'What is your occupation?'

7272.text: that you shall say, 'Your servants have been keepers of livestock from our youth even until now, both we, and our fathers:' that you may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians."

7273.text: Then Joseph went in and told Pharaoh, and said, "My father and my brothers, with their flocks, their herds, and all that they own, have come out of the land of Canaan; and behold, they are in the land of Goshen."

7274.text: From among his brothers he took five men, and presented them to Pharaoh.

7275.text: Pharaoh said to his brothers, "What is your occupation?" They said to Pharaoh, "Your servants are shepherds, both we, and our fathers."

7276.text: They said to Pharaoh, "We have come to live as foreigners in the land, for there is no pasture for your servants' flocks. For the famine is severe in the land of Canaan. Now therefore, please let your servants dwell in the land of Goshen."

7277.text: Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, "Your father and your brothers have come to you.

7278.text: The land of Egypt is before you. Make your father and your brothers dwell in the best of the land. Let them dwell in the land of Goshen. If you know any able men among them, then put them in charge of my livestock."

7279.text: Joseph brought in Jacob, his father, and set him before Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.

7280.text: Pharaoh said to Jacob, "How many are the days of the years of your life?"

7281.text: Jacob said to Pharaoh, "The days of the years of my pilgrimage are one hundred thirty years. Few and evil have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not attained to the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage."

7282.text: Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from the presence of Pharaoh.

7283.text: Joseph placed his father and his brothers, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.

7284.text: Joseph nourished his father, his brothers, and all of his father's household, with bread, according to their families.

7285.text: There was no bread in all the land; for the famine was very severe, so that the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan fainted by reason of the famine.

7286.text: Joseph gathered up all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the grain which they bought: and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh's house.

7287.text: When the money was all spent in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph, and said, "Give us bread, for why should we die in your presence? For our money fails."

7288.text: Joseph said, "Give me your livestock; and I will give you food for your livestock, if your money is gone."

7289.text: They brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for the horses, and for the flocks, and for the herds, and for the donkeys: and he fed them with bread in exchange for all their livestock for that year.

7290.text: When that year was ended, they came to him the second year, and said to him, "We will not hide from my lord how our money is all spent, and the herds of livestock are my lord's. There is nothing left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands.

7291.text: Why should we die before your eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants to Pharaoh. Give us seed, that we may live, and not die, and that the land won't be desolate."

7292.text: So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, for the Egyptians sold every man his field, because the famine was severe on them, and the land became Pharaoh's.

7293.text: As for the people, he moved them to the cities from one end of the border of Egypt even to the other end of it.

7294.text: Only he did not buy the land of the priests, for the priests had a portion from Pharaoh, and ate their portion which Pharaoh gave them. That is why they did not sell their land.

7295.text: Then Joseph said to the people, "Behold, I have bought you and your land today for Pharaoh. Behold, here is seed for you, and you shall sow the land.

7296.text: It will happen at the harvests, that you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh, and four parts will be your own, for seed of the field, for your food, for them of your households, and for food for your little ones."

7297.text: They said, "You have saved our lives! Let us find favor in the sight of my lord, and we will be Pharaoh's servants."

7298.text: Joseph made it a statute concerning the land of Egypt to this day, that Pharaoh should have the fifth. Only the land of the priests alone did not become Pharaoh's.

7299.text: Israel lived in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; and they got themselves possessions therein, and were fruitful, and multiplied exceedingly.

7300.text: Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years. So the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were one hundred forty-seven years.

7301.text: The time drew near that Israel must die, and he called his son Joseph, and said to him, "If now I have found favor in your sight, please put your hand under my thigh, and deal kindly and truly with me. Please do not bury me in Egypt,

7302.text: but when I sleep with my fathers, you shall carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in their burying place." He said, "I will do as you have said."

7303.text: He said, "Swear to me," and he swore to him. Israel bowed himself on the bed's head.

7304.text: It happened after these things, that someone said to Joseph, "Behold, your father is sick." He took with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.

7305.text: Someone told Jacob, and said, "Behold, your son Joseph comes to you," and Israel strengthened himself, and sat on the bed.

7306.text: Jacob said to Joseph, "God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,

7307.text: and said to me, 'Behold, I will make you fruitful, and multiply you, and I will make of you a company of peoples, and will give this land to your seed after you for an everlasting possession.'

7308.text: Now your two sons, who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came to you into Egypt, are mine; Ephraim and Manasseh, even as Reuben and Simeon, will be mine.

7309.text: Your issue, whom you become the father of after them, will be yours. They will be called after the name of their brothers in their inheritance.

7310.text: As for me, when I came from Paddan, Rachel died by me in the land of Canaan in the way, when there was still some distance to come to Ephrath, and I buried her there in the way to Ephrath (the same is Bethlehem)."

7311.text: Israel saw Joseph's sons, and said, "Who are these?"

7312.text: Joseph said to his father, "They are my sons, whom God has given me here." He said, "Please bring them to me, and I will bless them."

7313.text: Now the eyes of Israel were dim for age, so that he couldn't see. He brought them near to him; and he kissed them, and embraced them.

7314.text: Israel said to Joseph, "I did not think I would see your face, and behold, God has let me see your seed also."

7315.text: Joseph brought them out from between his knees, and he bowed himself with his face to the earth.

7316.text: Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel's left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel's right hand, and brought them near to him.

7317.text: Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it on Ephraim's head, who was the younger, and his left hand on Manasseh's head, guiding his hands knowingly, for Manasseh was the firstborn.

7318.text: He blessed Joseph, and said, "The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac did walk, the God who has fed me all my life long to this day,

7319.text: the angel who has redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads, and let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac. Let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth."

7320.text: When Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand on the head of Ephraim, it displeased him. He held up his father's hand, to remove it from Ephraim's head to Manasseh's head.

7321.text: Joseph said to his father, "Not so, my father; for this is the firstborn; put your right hand on his head."

7322.text: His father refused, and said, "I know, my son, I know. He also will become a people, and he also will be great. However, his younger brother will be greater than he, and his seed will become a multitude of nations."

7323.text: He blessed them that day, saying, "In you will Israel bless, saying, 'God make you as Ephraim and as Manasseh'" He set Ephraim before Manasseh.

7324.text: Israel said to Joseph, "Behold, I am dying, but God will be with you, and bring you again to the land of your fathers.

7325.text: Moreover I have given to you one portion above your brothers, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow."

7326.text: Jacob called to his sons, and said: "Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which will happen to you in the days to come.

7327.text: Assemble yourselves, and hear, you sons of Jacob. Listen to Israel, your father.

7328.text: "Reuben, you are my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength; excelling in dignity, and excelling in power.

7329.text: Boiling over as water, you shall not excel; because you went up to your father's bed, then defiled it. He went up to my couch.

7330.text: "Simeon and Levi are brothers. Their swords are weapons of violence.

7331.text: My soul, do not come into their council. My glory, do not be united to their assembly; for in their anger they killed men. In their self-will they hamstrung cattle.

7332.text: Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel. I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel.

7333.text: "Judah, your brothers will praise you. Your hand will be on the neck of your enemies. Your father's sons will bow down before you.

7334.text: Judah is a lion's cub. From the prey, my son, you have gone up. He stooped down, he crouched as a lion, as a lioness. Who will rouse him up?

7335.text: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until he comes to whom it belongs. To him will the obedience of the peoples be.

7336.text: Binding his foal to the vine, his donkey's colt to the choice vine; he has washed his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes.

7337.text: His eyes will be red with wine, his teeth white with milk.

7338.text: "Zebulun will dwell at the haven of the sea. He will be for a haven of ships. His border will be on Sidon.

7339.text: "Issachar is a strong donkey, lying down between the saddlebags.

7340.text: He saw a resting place, that it was good, the land, that it was pleasant. He bows his shoulder to the burden, and becomes a servant doing forced labor.

7341.text: "Dan will judge his people, as one of the tribes of Israel.

7342.text: Dan will be a serpent in the way, an adder in the path, That bites the horse's heels, so that his rider falls backward.

7343.text: I have waited for your salvation, Lord.

7344.text: "A troop will press on Gad, but he will press on their heel.

7345.text: "Asher's food will be rich. He will yield royal dainties.

7346.text: "Naphtali is a doe set free, who bears beautiful fawns.

7347.text: "Joseph is a fruitful vine, a fruitful vine by a spring. His branches run over the wall.

7348.text: The archers have sorely grieved him, shot at him, and persecute him:

7349.text: But his bow remained strong. The arms of his hands were made strong, by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob, (from there is the shepherd, the stone of Israel),

7350.text: even by the God of your father, who will help you; by the Almighty, who will bless you, with blessings of heaven above, blessings of the deep that lies below, blessings of the breasts, and of the womb.

7351.text: The blessings of your father have prevailed above the blessings of your ancestors, above the boundaries of the ancient hills. They will be on the head of Joseph, on the crown of the head of him who is separated from his brothers.

7352.text: "Benjamin is a ravenous wolf. In the morning he will devour the prey. At evening he will divide the spoil."

7353.text: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what their father spoke to them and blessed them. He blessed everyone according to his blessing.

7354.text: He instructed them, and said to them, "I am to be gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,

7355.text: in the cave that is in the field of Machpelah, which is before Mamre, in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought with the field from Ephron the Hittite as a burial place.

7356.text: There they buried Abraham and Sarah, his wife. There they buried Isaac and Rebekah, his wife, and there I buried Leah:

7357.text: the field and the cave that is therein, which was purchased from the children of Heth."

7358.text: When Jacob made an end of charging his sons, he gathered up his feet into the bed, and yielded up the spirit, and was gathered to his people.

7359.text: Joseph fell on his father's face, wept on him, and kissed him.

7360.text: Joseph commanded his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father; and the physicians embalmed Israel.

7361.text: Forty days were fulfilled for him, for that is how many the days it takes to embalm. The Egyptians wept for him for seventy days.

7362.text: When the days of weeping for him were past, Joseph spoke to the house of Pharaoh, saying, "If now I have found favor in your eyes, please speak in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,

7363.text: 'My father made me swear, saying, "Behold, I am dying. Bury me in my grave which I have dug for myself in the land of Canaan." Now therefore, please let me go up and bury my father, and I will come again.'"

7364.text: Pharaoh said, "Go up, and bury your father, just like he made you swear."

7365.text: Joseph went up to bury his father; and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, all the elders of the land of Egypt,

7366.text: all the house of Joseph, his brothers, and his father's house. Only their little ones, their flocks, and their herds, they left in the land of Goshen.

7367.text: There went up with him both chariots and horsemen. It was a very great company.

7368.text: They came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and there they lamented with a very great and sore lamentation. He mourned for his father seven days.

7369.text: When the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning in the floor of Atad, they said, "This is a grievous mourning by the Egyptians." Therefore, its name was called Abel Mizraim, which is beyond the Jordan.

7370.text: His sons did to him just as he commanded them,

7371.text: for his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field, for a possession of a burial site, from Ephron the Hittite, before Mamre.

7372.text: Joseph returned into Egypt-he, and his brothers, and all that went up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.

7373.text: When Joseph's brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, "It may be that Joseph will hate us, and will fully pay us back for all of the evil which we did to him."

7374.text: They sent a message to Joseph, saying, "Your father commanded before he died, saying,

7375.text: 'You shall tell Joseph, "Now please forgive the disobedience of your brothers, and their sin, because they did evil to you."' Now, please forgive the disobedience of the servants of the God of your father." Joseph wept when they spoke to him.

7376.text: His brothers also went and fell down before his face; and they said, "Behold, we are your servants."

7377.text: Joseph said to them, "Do not be afraid, for am I in the place of God?

7378.text: As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save many people alive.

7379.text: Now therefore do not be afraid. I will nourish you and your little ones." He comforted them, and spoke kindly to them.

7380.text: Joseph lived in Egypt, he, and his father's house. Joseph lived one hundred ten years.

7381.text: Joseph saw Ephraim's children to the third generation. The children also of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were born on Joseph's knees.

7382.text: Joseph said to his brothers, "I am dying, but God will surely visit you, and bring you up out of this land to the land which he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob."

7383.text: Joseph took an oath of the children of Israel, saying, "God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from here."

7384.text: So Joseph died, being one hundred ten years old, and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

7385.text: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt (every man and his household came with Jacob):

7388.text: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.

7389.text: All the souls who came out of Jacob's body were seventy-five souls, and Joseph was in Egypt already.

7390.text: Joseph died, as did all his brothers, and all that generation.

7391.text: The children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and grew exceedingly mighty; and the land was filled with them.

7392.text: Now there arose a new king over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.

7393.text: He said to his people, "Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we.

7394.text: Come, let us deal wisely with them, lest they multiply, and it happen that when any war breaks out, they also join themselves to our enemies, and fight against us, and escape out of the land."

7395.text: Therefore they set taskmasters over them to afflict them with their burdens. They built storage cities for Pharaoh: Pithom and Raamses.

7396.text: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and the more they spread out. They were grieved because of the children of Israel.

7397.text: The Egyptians ruthlessly made the children of Israel serve,

7398.text: and they made their lives bitter with hard service, in mortar and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field, all their service, in which they ruthlessly made them serve.

7399.text: The king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah,

7400.text: and he said, "When you perform the duty of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them on the birth stool; if it is a son, then you shall kill him; but if it is a daughter, then she shall live."

7401.text: But the midwives feared God, and did not do what the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the baby boys alive.

7402.text: The king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said to them, "Why have you done this thing, and have saved the boys alive?"

7403.text: The midwives said to Pharaoh, "Because the Hebrew women aren't like the Egyptian women; for they are vigorous, and give birth before the midwife comes to them."

7404.text: God dealt well with the midwives, and the people multiplied, and grew very mighty.

7405.text: It happened, because the midwives feared God, that he gave them families.

7406.text: Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, "You shall cast every son who is born into the river, and every daughter you shall save alive."

7407.text: A man of the house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi as his wife.

7408.text: The woman conceived, and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

7409.text: When she could no longer hide him, she took a papyrus basket for him, and coated it with tar and with pitch. She put the child in it, and laid it in the reeds by the river's bank.

7410.text: His sister stood far off, to see what would be done to him.

7411.text: Pharaoh's daughter came down to bathe at the river. Her maidens walked along by the riverside. She saw the basket among the reeds, and sent her handmaid to get it.

7412.text: She opened it, and saw the child, and behold, the baby cried. And she had compassion on him, and said, "This is one of the Hebrews' children."

7413.text: Then his sister said to Pharaoh's daughter, "Should I go and call a nurse for you from the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for you?"

7414.text: Pharaoh's daughter said to her, "Go." The maiden went and called the child's mother.

7415.text: Pharaoh's daughter said to her, "Take this child away, and nurse him for me, and I will give you your wages." The woman took the child, and nursed it.

7416.text: The child grew, and she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, and said, "Because I drew him out of the water."

7417.text: It happened in those days, when Moses had grown up, that he went out to his brothers, and looked at their burdens. He saw an Egyptian striking a Hebrew, one of his brothers.

7418.text: He looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no one, he killed the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.

7419.text: He went out the second day, and behold, two men of the Hebrews were fighting with each other. He said to him who did the wrong, "Why do you strike your fellow?"

7420.text: He said, "Who made you a prince and a judge over us? Do you plan to kill me, as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?" Moses was afraid, and said, "Surely this thing is known."

7421.text: Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and lived in the land of Midian, and he sat down by a well.

7422.text: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters. They came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.

7423.text: The shepherds came and drove them away; but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.

7424.text: When they came to Reuel, their father, he said, "How is it that you have returned so early today?"

7425.text: They said, "An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and moreover he drew water for us, and watered the flock."

7426.text: He said to his daughters, "Where is he? Why is it that you have left the man? Call him, that he may eat bread."

7427.text: Moses was content to dwell with the man. He gave Moses Zipporah, his daughter.

7428.text: She bore a son, and he named him Gershom, for he said, "I have lived as a foreigner in a foreign land."

7429.text: It happened in the course of those many days, that the king of Egypt died, and the children of Israel sighed because of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up to God because of the bondage.

7430.text: God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

7431.text: God saw the children of Israel, and God was concerned about them.

7432.text: Now Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro, his father-in-law, the priest of Midian, and he led the flock to the back of the wilderness, and came to God's mountain, to Horeb.

7433.text: The angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush. He looked, and behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.

7434.text: Moses said, "I will turn aside now, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt."

7435.text: When the Lord saw that he turned aside to see, God called to him out of the midst of the bush, and said, "Moses! Moses!" He said, "Here I am."

7436.text: He said, "Do not come close. Take your sandals off of your feet, for the place you are standing on is holy ground."

7437.text: Moreover he said, "I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob." Moses hid his face; for he was afraid to look at God.

7438.text: The Lord said, "I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and have heard their cry because of their taskmasters, for I know their sorrows.

7439.text: I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land to a good and large land, to a land flowing with milk and honey; to the place of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.

7440.text: Now, behold, the cry of the children of Israel has come to me. Moreover I have seen the oppression with which the Egyptians oppress them.

7441.text: Come now therefore, and I will send you to Pharaoh, that you may bring forth my people, the children of Israel, out of Egypt."

7442.text: Moses said to God, "Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt?"

7443.text: He said, "Certainly I will be with you. This will be the token to you, that I have sent you: when you have brought forth the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God on this mountain."

7444.text: Moses said to God, "Behold, when I come to the children of Israel, and tell them, 'The God of your fathers has sent me to you;' and they ask me, 'What is his name?' What should I tell them?"

7445.text: God said to Moses, "I AM WHO I AM," and he said, "You shall tell the children of Israel this: 'I AM has sent me to you.'"

7446.text: God said moreover to Moses, "You shall tell the children of Israel this, 'The Lord, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.' This is my name forever, and this is my memorial to all generations.

7447.text: Go, and gather the elders of the children of Israel together, and tell them, 'The Lord, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, has appeared to me, saying, "I have surely visited you, and seen that which is done to you in Egypt;

7448.text: and I have said, I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt to the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, to a land flowing with milk and honey."'

7449.text: They will listen to your voice, and you shall come, you and the elders of Israel, to the king of Egypt, and you shall tell him, 'The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us. Now please let us go three days' journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to the Lord, our God.'

7450.text: I know that the king of Egypt won't give you permission to go, except by a mighty hand.

7451.text: I will put forth my hand and strike Egypt with all my wonders which I will do in its midst, and after that he will let you go.

7452.text: I will give this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, and it will happen that when you go, you shall not go empty-handed.

7453.text: But every woman shall ask of her neighbor, and of her who visits her house, jewels of silver, jewels of gold, and clothing; and you shall put them on your sons, and on your daughters. You shall despoil the Egyptians.

7454.text: Moses answered, "But, behold, they will not believe me, nor listen to my voice; for they will say, 'The Lord has not appeared to you.'"

7455.text: The Lord said to him, "What is that in your hand?" He said, "A rod."

7456.text: He said, "Throw it on the ground." He threw it on the ground, and it became a snake; and Moses ran away from it.

7457.text: The Lord said to Moses, "Put forth your hand, and take it by the tail." He put forth his hand, and laid hold of it, and it became a rod in his hand.

7458.text: "That they may believe that the Lord, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has appeared to you."

7459.text: The Lord said furthermore to him, "Now put your hand inside your cloak." He put his hand inside his cloak, and when he took it out from his cloak, behold, his hand was leprous, as white as snow.

7460.text: He said, "Put your hand inside your cloak again." He put his hand inside his cloak again, and when he took it out of his cloak, behold, it had turned again as his other flesh.

7461.text: "It will happen, if they will neither believe you nor listen to the voice of the first sign, that they will believe the voice of the latter sign.

7462.text: It will happen, if they will not believe even these two signs, neither listen to your voice, that you shall take of the water of the river, and pour it on the dry land. The water which you take out of the river will become blood on the dry land."

7463.text: Moses said to the Lord, "Oh, Lord, I am not eloquent, neither before now, nor since you have spoken to your servant; for I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue."

7464.text: The Lord said to him, "Who made man's mouth? Or who makes one mute, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Isn't it I, the Lord?

7465.text: Now therefore go, and I will be with your mouth, and teach you what you shall speak."

7466.text: He said, "Oh, Lord, please send someone else."

7467.text: The anger of the Lord was kindled against Moses, and he said, "What about Aaron, your brother, the Levite? I know that he can speak well. Also, behold, he comes forth to meet you. When he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.

7468.text: You shall speak to him, and put the words in his mouth. I will be with your mouth, and with his mouth, and will teach you what you shall do.

7469.text: He will be your spokesman to the people; and it will happen, that he will be to you a mouth, and you will be to him as God.

7470.text: You shall take this rod in your hand, with which you shall do the signs."

7471.text: Moses went and returned to Jethro his father-in-law, and said to him, "Please let me go and return to my brothers who are in Egypt, and see whether they are still alive." Jethro said to Moses, "Go in peace."

7472.text: The Lord said to Moses in Midian, "Go, return into Egypt; for all the men who sought your life are dead."

7473.text: Moses took his wife and his sons, and set them on a donkey, and he returned to the land of Egypt. Moses took God's rod in his hand.

7474.text: The Lord said to Moses, "When you go back into Egypt, see that you do before Pharaoh all the wonders which I have put in your hand, but I will harden his heart and he will not let the people go.

7475.text: You shall tell Pharaoh, 'Thus says the Lord, Israel is my son, my firstborn,

7476.text: and I have said to you, "Let my son go, that he may serve me;" and you have refused to let him go. Behold, I will kill your son, your firstborn.'"

7477.text: It happened on the way at a lodging place, that the Lord met him and wanted to kill him.

7478.text: Then Zipporah took a flint, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet; and she said, "Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me."

7479.text: So he let him alone. Then she said, "You are a bridegroom of blood," because of the circumcision.

7480.text: The Lord said to Aaron, "Go into the wilderness to meet Moses." He went, and met him on God's mountain, and kissed him.

7481.text: Moses told Aaron all the words of the Lord with which he had sent him, and all the signs with which he had instructed him.

7482.text: Moses and Aaron went and gathered together all the elders of the children of Israel.

7483.text: Aaron spoke all the words which the Lord had spoken to Moses, and did the signs in the sight of the people.

7484.text: The people believed, and when they heard that the Lord had visited the children of Israel, and that he had seen their affliction, then they bowed their heads and worshiped.

7485.text: Afterward Moses and Aaron came, and said to Pharaoh, "This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says, 'Let my people go, that they may hold a feast to me in the wilderness.'"

7486.text: Pharaoh said, "Who is the Lord, that I should listen to his voice to let Israel go? I do not know the Lord, and moreover I will not let Israel go."

7487.text: They said, "The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Please let us go three days' journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice to the Lord, our God, lest he fall on us with pestilence, or with the sword."

7488.text: The king of Egypt said to them, "Why do you, Moses and Aaron, separate the people from their work? Get back to your burdens!"

7489.text: Pharaoh said, "Behold, the people of the land are now many, and you make them rest from their burdens."

7490.text: The same day Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters of the people, and their officers, saying,

7491.text: "You shall no longer give the people straw to make brick, as before. Let them go and gather straw for themselves.

7492.text: The number of the bricks, which they made before, you require from them. You shall not diminish anything of it, for they are idle; therefore they cry, saying, 'Let us go and sacrifice to our God.'

7493.text: Let heavier work be laid on the men, that they may regard it; and do not let them regard lying words."

7494.text: The taskmasters of the people went out, and their officers, and they spoke to the people, saying, This is what Pharaoh says: "I will not give you straw.

7495.text: Go yourselves, get straw where you can find it, for nothing of your work shall be diminished."

7496.text: So the people were scattered abroad throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.

7497.text: The taskmasters were urgent saying, "Fulfill your work quota daily, as when there was straw given to you!"

7498.text: The officers of the children of Israel, whom Pharaoh's taskmasters had set over them, were beaten, and demanded, "Why haven't you fulfilled your quota both yesterday and today, in making brick as before?"

7499.text: Then the officers of the children of Israel came and cried to Pharaoh, saying, "Why do you deal this way with your servants?

7500.text: No straw is given to your servants, and they tell us, 'Make brick!' and behold, your servants are beaten; but the fault is in your own people."

7501.text: But he said, "You are idle! You are idle! Therefore you say, 'Let us go and sacrifice to the Lord.'

7502.text: Go therefore now, and work, for no straw shall be given to you, yet you shall deliver the same number of bricks!"

7503.text: The officers of the children of Israel saw that they were in trouble, when it was said, "You shall not diminish anything from your daily quota of bricks!"

7504.text: They met Moses and Aaron, who stood in the way, as they came forth from Pharaoh:

7505.text: and they said to them, "May the Lord look at you, and judge, because you have made us a stench to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to kill us."

7506.text: Moses returned to the Lord, and said, "Lord, why have you brought trouble on this people? Why is it that you have sent me?

7507.text: For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has brought trouble on this people; neither have you delivered your people at all."

7508.text: The Lord said to Moses, "Now you shall see what I will do to Pharaoh, for by a strong hand he shall let them go, and by a strong hand he shall drive them out of his land."

7509.text: God spoke to Moses, and said to him, "I am the Lord;

7510.text: and I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, as God Almighty; but by my name the Lord I was not known to them.

7511.text: I have also established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their travels, in which they lived as foreigners.

7512.text: Moreover I have heard the groaning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians keep in bondage, and I have remembered my covenant.

7513.text: Therefore tell the children of Israel, 'I am the Lord, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will rid you out of their bondage, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm, and with great judgments:

7514.text: and I will take you to me for a people, and I will be to you a God; and you shall know that I am the Lord your God, who brings you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians.

7515.text: I will bring you into the land which I swore to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will give it to you for a heritage: I am the Lord.'"

7516.text: Moses spoke so to the children of Israel, but they did not listen to Moses for anguish of spirit, and for cruel bondage.

7517.text: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,

7518.text: "Go in, speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land."

7519.text: Moses spoke before the Lord, saying, "Behold, the children of Israel haven't listened to me. How then shall Pharaoh listen to me, who am of uncircumcised lips?"

7520.text: The Lord spoke to Moses and to Aaron, and gave them a command to the children of Israel, and to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.

7521.text: These are the heads of their fathers' houses. The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, and Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi; these are the families of Reuben.

7522.text: The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman; these are the families of Simeon.

7523.text: These are the names of the sons of Levi according to their generations: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari; and the years of the life of Levi were one hundred thirty-seven years.

7524.text: The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, according to their families.

7525.text: The sons of Kohath: Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel; and the years of the life of Kohath were one hundred thirty-three years.

7526.text: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to their generations.

7527.text: Amram took Jochebed his father's sister to himself as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram were a hundred and thirty-seven years.

7528.text: The sons of Izhar: Korah, and Nepheg, and Zichri.

7529.text: The sons of Uzziel: Mishael, and Elzaphan, and Sithri.

7530.text: Aaron took Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab, the sister of Nahshon, as his wife; and she bore him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

7531.text: The sons of Korah: Assir, and Elkanah, and Abiasaph; these are the families of the Korahites.

7532.text: Eleazar Aaron's son took one of the daughters of Putiel as his wife; and she bore him Phinehas. These are the heads of the fathers' houses of the Levites according to their families.

7533.text: These are that Aaron and Moses, to whom the Lord said, "Bring out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt according to their armies."

7534.text: These are those who spoke to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring out the children of Israel from Egypt. These are that Moses and Aaron.

7535.text: It happened on the day when the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,

7536.text: that the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, "I am the Lord. Speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I speak to you."

7537.text: Moses said before the Lord, "Behold, I am of uncircumcised lips, and how shall Pharaoh listen to me?"

7538.text: The Lord said to Moses, "Behold, I have made you as God to Pharaoh; and Aaron your brother shall be your prophet.

7539.text: You shall speak all that I command you; and Aaron your brother shall speak to Pharaoh, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.

7540.text: I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.

7541.text: But Pharaoh will not listen to you, and I will lay my hand on Egypt, and bring forth my armies, my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.

7542.text: The Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, when I stretch forth my hand on Egypt, and bring out the children of Israel from among them."

7543.text: Moses and Aaron did so. As the Lord commanded them, so they did.

7544.text: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

7545.text: The Lord spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

7546.text: "When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, 'Perform a miracle!' then you shall tell Aaron, 'Take your rod, and cast it down before Pharaoh, that it become a serpent.'"

7547.text: Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh, and they did so, as the Lord had commanded: and Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.

7548.text: Then Pharaoh also called for the wise men and the sorcerers. They also, the magicians of Egypt, did in like manner with their enchantments.

7549.text: For they cast down every man his rod, and they became serpents: but Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods.

7550.text: Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them; as the Lord had spoken.

7551.text: The Lord said to Moses, "Pharaoh's heart is stubborn. He refuses to let the people go.

7552.text: Go to Pharaoh in the morning. Behold, he goes out to the water; and you shall stand by the river's bank to meet him; and the rod which was turned to a serpent you shall take in your hand.

7553.text: You shall tell him, 'The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying, "Let my people go, that they may serve me in the wilderness:" and behold, until now you haven't listened.

7554.text: Thus says the Lord, "In this you shall know that I am the Lord. Behold, I will strike with the rod that is in my hand on the waters which are in the river, and they shall be turned to blood.

7555.text: The fish that are in the river shall die, and the river shall become foul; and the Egyptians shall loathe to drink water from the river."'"

7556.text: The Lord said to Moses, "Tell Aaron, 'Take your rod, and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, over their streams, and over their pools, and over all their ponds of water, that they may become blood; and there shall be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood and in vessels of stone.'"

7557.text: Moses and Aaron did so, as the Lord commanded; and he lifted up the rod, and struck the waters that were in the river, in the sight of Pharaoh, and in the sight of his servants; and all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood.

7558.text: The fish that were in the river died; and the river became foul, and the Egyptians couldn't drink water from the river; and the blood was throughout all the land of Egypt.

7559.text: The magicians of Egypt did in like manner with their enchantments; and Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them; as the Lord had spoken.

7560.text: Pharaoh turned and went into his house, neither did he lay even this to heart.

7561.text: All the Egyptians dug around the river for water to drink; for they couldn't drink of the water of the river.

7562.text: Seven days were fulfilled, after the Lord had struck the river.

7563.text: The Lord spoke to Moses, Go in to Pharaoh, and tell him, "This is what the Lord says, 'Let my people go, that they may serve me.

7564.text: If you refuse to let them go, behold, I will plague all your borders with frogs:

7565.text: and the river shall swarm with frogs, which shall go up and come into your house, and into your bedchamber, and on your bed, and into the house of your servants, and on your people, and into your ovens, and into your kneading troughs:

7566.text: and the frogs shall come up both on you, and on your people, and on all your servants.'"

7567.text: The Lord said to Moses, "Tell Aaron, 'Stretch forth your hand with your rod over the rivers, over the streams, and over the pools, and cause frogs to come up on the land of Egypt.'"

7568.text: Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt; and the frogs came up, and covered the land of Egypt.

7569.text: The magicians did in like manner with their enchantments, and brought up frogs on the land of Egypt.

7570.text: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron, and said, "Entreat the Lord, that he take away the frogs from me, and from my people; and I will let the people go, that they may sacrifice to the Lord."

7571.text: Moses said to Pharaoh, "I give you the honor of setting the time that I should pray for you, and for your servants, and for your people, that the frogs be destroyed from you and your houses, and remain in the river only."

7572.text: He said, "Tomorrow." He said, "Be it according to your word, that you may know that there is none like the Lord our God.

7573.text: The frogs shall depart from you, and from your houses, and from your servants, and from your people. They shall remain in the river only."

7574.text: Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh, and Moses cried to the Lord concerning the frogs which he had brought on Pharaoh.

7575.text: The Lord did according to the word of Moses, and the frogs died out of the houses, out of the courts, and out of the fields.

7576.text: They gathered them together in heaps, and the land stank.
