11348.text: but to the lady you shall do nothing; there is in the lady no sin worthy of death: for as when a man rises against his neighbor, and kills him, even so is this matter;

11349.text: for he found her in the field, the pledged to be married lady cried, and there was none to save her.

11350.text: If a man find a lady who is a virgin, who is not pledged to be married, and lay hold on her, and lie with her, and they be found;

11351.text: then the man who lay with her shall give to the lady's father fifty shekels of silver, and she shall be his wife, because he has humbled her; he may not put her away all his days.

11352.text: A man shall not take his father's wife, and shall not uncover his father's skirt.

11353.text: He who is wounded in the stones, or has his privy member cut off, shall not enter into the assembly of the Lord.

11354.text: No one of illegitimate birth shall enter into the assembly of the Lord; even to the tenth generation shall none of his enter into the assembly of the Lord.

11355.text: An Ammonite or a Moabite shall not enter into the assembly of the Lord; even to the tenth generation shall none belonging to them enter into the assembly of the Lord forever:

11356.text: because they did not meet you with bread and with water in the way, when you came forth out of Egypt, and because they hired against you Balaam the son of Beor from Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse you.

11357.text: Nevertheless the Lord your God wouldn't listen to Balaam; but the Lord your God turned the curse into a blessing to you, because the Lord your God loved you.

11358.text: You shall not seek their peace nor their prosperity all your days forever.

11359.text: You shall not abhor an Edomite; for he is your brother: you shall not abhor an Egyptian, because you lived as a foreigner in his land.

11360.text: The children of the third generation who are born to them shall enter into the assembly of the Lord.

11361.text: When you go forth in camp against your enemies, then you shall keep yourselves from every evil thing.

11362.text: If there is among you any man who is not clean by reason of that which happens him by night, then shall he go outside of the camp. He shall not come within the camp:

11363.text: but it shall be, when evening comes on, he shall bathe himself in water; and when the sun is down, he shall come within the camp.

11364.text: You shall have a place also outside of the camp, where you shall go outside there;

11365.text: and you shall have a spade among your tools; and it shall be, when you sit down outside, you shall dig therewith, and shall turn and cover that which comes from you:

11366.text: for the Lord your God walks in the midst of your camp, to deliver you, and to give up your enemies before you; therefore your camp shall be holy, that he may not see an unclean thing in you, and turn away from you.

11367.text: You shall not deliver to his master a servant who is escaped from his master to you:

11368.text: he shall dwell with you, in the midst of you, in the place which he shall choose within one of your gates, where it pleases him best: you shall not oppress him.

11369.text: There shall be no prostitute of the daughters of Israel, neither shall there be a sodomite of the sons of Israel.

11370.text: You shall not bring the hire of a prostitute, or the wages of a dog, into the house of the Lord your God for any vow: for even both these are an abomination to the Lord your God.

11371.text: You shall not lend on interest to your brother; interest of money, interest of food, interest of anything that is lent on interest:

11372.text: to a foreigner you may lend on interest; but to your brother you shall not lend on interest, that the Lord your God may bless you in all that you put your hand to, in the land where you go in to possess it.

11373.text: When you shall vow a vow to the Lord your God, you shall not be slack to pay it: for the Lord your God will surely require it of you; and it would be sin in you.

11374.text: But if you shall forbear to vow, it shall be no sin in you.

11375.text: That which is gone out of your lips you shall observe and do; according as you have vowed to the Lord your God, a freewill offering, which you have promised with your mouth.

11376.text: When you come into your neighbor's vineyard, then you may eat of grapes your fill at your own pleasure; but you shall not put any in your vessel.

11377.text: When you come into your neighbor's standing grain, then you may pluck the ears with your hand; but you shall not move a sickle to your neighbor's standing grain.

11378.text: When a man takes a wife, and marries her, then it shall be, if she find no favor in his eyes, because he has found some unseemly thing in her, that he shall write her a bill of divorce, and give it in her hand, and send her out of his house.

11379.text: When she is departed out of his house, she may go and be another man's wife.

11380.text: If the latter husband hate her, and write her a bill of divorce, and give it in her hand, and send her out of his house; or if the latter husband die, who took her to be his wife;

11381.text: her former husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after that she is defiled; for that is abomination before the Lord: and you shall not cause the land to sin, which the Lord your God gives you for an inheritance.

11382.text: When a man takes a new wife, he shall not go out in the army, neither shall he be assigned any business: he shall be free at home one year, and shall cheer his wife whom he has taken.

11383.text: No man shall take the mill or the upper millstone to pledge; for he takes a life in pledge.

11384.text: If a man be found stealing any of his brothers of the children of Israel, and he deal with him as a slave, or sell him; then that thief shall die: so you shall put away the evil from the midst of you.

11385.text: Take heed in the plague of leprosy, that you observe diligently, and do according to all that the priests the Levites shall teach you: as I commanded them, so you shall observe to do.

11386.text: Remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam, by the way as you came forth out of Egypt.

11387.text: When you do lend your neighbor any kind of loan, you shall not go into his house to get his pledge.

11388.text: You shall stand outside, and the man to whom you do lend shall bring forth the pledge outside to you.

11389.text: If he be a poor man, you shall not sleep with his pledge;

11390.text: you shall surely restore to him the pledge when the sun goes down, that he may sleep in his garment, and bless you: and it shall be righteousness to you before the Lord your God.

11391.text: You shall not oppress a hired servant who is poor and needy, whether he be of your brothers, or of your foreigners who are in your land within your gates:

11392.text: in his day you shall give him his hire, neither shall the sun go down on it; for he is poor, and sets his heart on it: lest he cry against you to the Lord, and it be sin to you.

11393.text: The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin.

11394.text: You shall not deprive the foreigner, or the fatherless of justice, nor take a widow's clothing in pledge;

11395.text: but you shall remember that you were a bondservant in Egypt, and the Lord your God redeemed you there: therefore I command you to do this thing.

11396.text: When you reap your harvest in your field, and have forgot a sheaf in the field, you shall not go again to get it: it shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the widow; that the Lord your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.

11397.text: When you beat your olive tree, you shall not go over the boughs again: it shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the widow.

11398.text: When you harvest your vineyard, you shall not glean it after yourselves: it shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the widow.

11399.text: You shall remember that you were a bondservant in the land of Egypt: therefore I command you to do this thing.

11400.text: If there is a controversy between men, and they come to judgment, and the judges judge them; then they shall justify the righteous, and condemn the wicked;

11401.text: and it shall be, if the wicked man be worthy to be beaten, that the judge shall cause him to lie down, and to be beaten before his face, according to his wickedness, by number.

11402.text: Forty stripes he may give him, he shall not exceed; lest, if he should exceed, and beat him above these with many stripes, then your brother should seem vile to you.

11403.text: You shall not muzzle the ox when he treads out the grain.

11404.text: If brothers dwell together, and one of them die, and have no son, the wife of the dead shall not be married outside to a stranger: her husband's brother shall go in to her, and take her to him as wife, and perform the duty of a husband's brother to her.

11405.text: It shall be, that the firstborn whom she bears shall succeed in the name of his brother who is dead, that his name not be blotted out of Israel.

11406.text: If the man doesn't want to take his brother's wife, then his brother's wife shall go up to the gate to the elders, and say, "My husband's brother refuses to raise up to his brother a name in Israel; he will not perform the duty of a husband's brother to me."

11407.text: Then the elders of his city shall call him, and speak to him: and if he stand, and say, "I do not want to take her";

11408.text: then his brother's wife shall come to him in the presence of the elders, and loose his shoe from off his foot, and spit in his face; and she shall answer and say, "So shall it be done to the man who does not build up his brother's house."

11409.text: His name shall be called in Israel, The house of him who has his shoe untied.

11410.text: When men strive together one with another, and the wife of the one draws near to deliver her husband out of the hand of him who strikes him, and puts forth her hand, and takes him by the secrets;

11411.text: then you shall cut off her hand, your eye shall have no pity.

11412.text: You shall not have in your bag diverse weights, a great and a small.

11413.text: You shall not have in your house diverse measures, a great and a small.

11414.text: You shall have a perfect and just weight. You shall have a perfect and just measure, that your days may be long in the land which the Lord your God gives you.

11415.text: For all who do such things, all who do unrighteously, are an abomination to the Lord your God.

11416.text: Remember what Amalek did to you by the way as you came forth out of Egypt;

11417.text: how he met you by the way, and struck the hindmost of you, all who were feeble behind you, when you were faint and weary; and he did not fear God.

11418.text: Therefore it shall be, when the Lord your God has given you rest from all your enemies all around, in the land which the Lord your God gives you for an inheritance to possess it, that you shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under the sky; you shall not forget.

11419.text: It shall be, when you have come in to the land which the Lord your God gives you for an inheritance, and possess it, and dwell therein,

11420.text: that you shall take of the first of all the fruit of the ground, which you shall bring in from your land that the Lord your God gives you; and you shall put it in a basket, and shall go to the place which the Lord your God shall choose, to cause his name to dwell there.

11421.text: You shall come to the priest who shall be in those days, and tell him, "I profess this day to the Lord your God, that I am come to the land which the Lord swore to our fathers to give us."

11422.text: The priest shall take the basket out of your hand, and set it down before the altar of the Lord your God.

11423.text: You shall answer and say before the Lord your God, "A Syrian ready to perish was my father; and he went down into Egypt, and lived there, few in number; and he became there a nation, great, mighty, and populous.

11424.text: The Egyptians dealt ill with us, and afflicted us, and laid on us hard bondage:

11425.text: and we cried to the Lord, the God of our fathers, and the Lord heard our voice, and saw our affliction, and our toil, and our oppression;

11426.text: and the Lord brought us forth out of Egypt with a mighty hand, and with an outstretched arm, and with great terror, and with signs, and with wonders;

11427.text: and he has brought us into this place, and has given us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.

11428.text: Now, behold, I have brought the first of the fruit of the ground, which you, Lord, have given me." You shall set it down before the Lord your God, and worship before the Lord your God.

11429.text: You shall rejoice in all the good which the Lord your God has given to you, and to your house, you, and the Levite, and the foreigner who is in the midst of you.

11430.text: When you have made an end of tithing all the tithe of your increase in the third year, which is the year of tithing, then you shall give it to the Levite, to the foreigner, to the fatherless, and to the widow, that they may eat within your gates, and be filled.

11431.text: You shall say before the Lord your God, "I have put away the holy things out of my house, and also have given them to the Levite, and to the foreigner, to the fatherless, and to the widow, according to all your commandment which you have commanded me: I have not transgressed any of your commandments, neither have I forgotten them:

11432.text: I have not eaten of it in my mourning, neither have I put away of it, being unclean, nor given of it for the dead: I have listened to the voice of the Lord my God; I have done according to all that you have commanded me.

11433.text: Look down from your holy habitation, from heaven, and bless your people Israel, and the ground which you have given us, as you swore to our fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey."

11434.text: This day the Lord your God commands you to do these statutes and ordinances: you shall therefore keep and do them with all your heart, and with all your soul.

11435.text: You have declared the Lord this day to be your God, and that you would walk in his ways, and keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his ordinances, and listen to his voice:

11436.text: and the Lord has declared you this day to be a people for his own possession, as he has promised you, and that you should keep all his commandments;

11437.text: and to make you high above all nations that he has made, in praise, and in name, and in honor; and that you may be a holy people to the Lord your God, as he has spoken.

11438.text: Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people, saying, "Keep all the commandment which I command you this day.

11439.text: It shall be on the day when you shall pass over the Jordan to the land which the Lord your God gives you, that you shall set yourself up great stones, and plaster them with plaster:

11440.text: and you shall write on them all the words of this law, when you have passed over; that you may go in to the land which the Lord your God gives you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as the Lord, the God of your fathers, has promised you.

11441.text: It shall be, when you have passed over the Jordan, that you shall set up these stones, which I command you this day, in Mount Ebal, and you shall plaster them with plaster.

11442.text: There you shall build an altar to the Lord your God, an altar of stones: you shall lift up no iron on them.

11443.text: You shall build the altar of the Lord your God of uncut stones; and you shall offer burnt offerings thereon to the Lord your God:

11444.text: and you shall sacrifice peace offerings, and shall eat there; and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God.

11445.text: You shall write on the stones all the words of this law very plainly."

11446.text: Moses and the priests the Levites spoke to all Israel, saying, "Keep silence, and listen, Israel: this day you have become the people of the Lord your God.

11447.text: You shall therefore obey the voice of the Lord your God, and do his commandments and his statutes, which I command you this day."

11448.text: Moses commanded the people the same day, saying,

11449.text: "These shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people, when you have passed over the Jordan: Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Joseph, and Benjamin.

11450.text: These shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, and Asher, and Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.

11451.text: The Levites shall answer, and tell all the men of Israel with a loud voice,

11452.text: 'Cursed is the man who makes an engraved or molten image, an abomination to the Lord, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and sets it up in secret.' All the people shall answer and say, 'Amen.'

11453.text: 'Cursed is he who sets light by his father or his mother.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

11454.text: 'Cursed is he who removes his neighbor's landmark.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

11455.text: 'Cursed is he who makes the blind to wander out of the way.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

11456.text: 'Cursed is he who wrests the justice due the foreigner, fatherless, and widow.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

11457.text: 'Cursed is he who lies with his father's wife, because he has uncovered his father's skirt.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

11458.text: 'Cursed is he who lies with any kind of animal.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

11459.text: 'Cursed is he who lies with his sister, the daughter of his father, or the daughter of his mother.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

11460.text: 'Cursed is he who lies with his mother-in-law.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

11461.text: 'Cursed is he who strikes his neighbor in secret.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

11462.text: 'Cursed is he who takes a bribe to kill an innocent person.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

11463.text: 'Cursed is he who doesn't confirm the words of this law to do them.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'"

11464.text: It shall happen, if you shall listen diligently to the voice of the Lord your God, to observe to do all his commandments which I command you this day, that the Lord your God will set you on high above all the nations of the earth:

11465.text: and all these blessings shall come on you, and overtake you, if you shall listen to the voice of the Lord your God.

11466.text: You shall be blessed in the city, and you shall be blessed in the field.

11467.text: You shall be blessed in the fruit of your body, the fruit of your ground, the fruit of your animals, the increase of your livestock, and the young of your flock.

11468.text: Your basket and your kneading trough shall be blessed.

11469.text: You shall be blessed when you come in, and you shall be blessed when you go out.

11470.text: The Lord will cause your enemies who rise up against you to be struck before you. They will come out against you one way, and will flee before you seven ways.

11471.text: The Lord will command the blessing on you in your barns, and in all that you put your hand to; and he will bless you in the land which the Lord your God gives you.

11472.text: The Lord will establish you for a holy people to himself, as he has sworn to you; if you shall keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and walk in his ways.

11473.text: All the peoples of the earth shall see that you are called by the name of the Lord; and they shall be afraid of you.

11474.text: The Lord will make you plenteous for good, in the fruit of your body, and in the fruit of your livestock, and in the fruit of your ground, in the land which the Lord swore to your fathers to give you.

11475.text: The Lord will open to you his good treasure in the sky, to give the rain of your land in its season, and to bless all the work of your hand: and you shall lend to many nations, and you shall not borrow.

11476.text: The Lord will make you the head, and not the tail; and you shall be above only, and you shall not be beneath; if you shall listen to the commandments of the Lord your God, which I command you this day, to observe and to do,

11477.text: and shall not turn aside from any of the words which I command you this day, to the right hand, or to the left, to go after other gods to serve them.

11478.text: But it shall come to pass, if you will not listen to the voice of the Lord your God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command you this day, that all these curses shall come on you, and overtake you.

11479.text: You shall be cursed in the city, and you shall be cursed in the field.

11480.text: Your basket and your kneading trough shall be cursed.

11481.text: The fruit of your body, the fruit of your ground, the increase of your livestock, and the young of your flock shall be cursed.

11482.text: You shall be cursed when you come in, and you shall be cursed when you go out.

11483.text: The Lord will send on you cursing, confusion, and rebuke, in all that you put your hand to do, until you are destroyed, and until you perish quickly; because of the evil of your doings, by which you have forsaken me.

11484.text: The Lord will make the pestilence cling to you, until he has consumed you from off the land, where you go in to possess it.

11485.text: The Lord will strike you with consumption, and with fever, and with inflammation, and with fiery heat, and with the sword, and with blight, and with mildew; and they shall pursue you until you perish.

11486.text: Your sky that is over your head shall be brass, and the earth that is under you shall be iron.

11487.text: The Lord will make the rain of your land powder and dust: from the sky shall it come down on you, until you are destroyed.

11488.text: The Lord will cause you to be struck before your enemies; you shall go out one way against them, and shall flee seven ways before them: and you shall be tossed back and forth among all the kingdoms of the earth.

11489.text: Your dead body shall be food to all birds of the sky, and to the animals of the earth; and there shall be none to frighten them away.

11490.text: The Lord will strike you with the boil of Egypt, and with the tumors, and with the scurvy, and with the itch, of which you can not be healed.

11491.text: The Lord will strike you with madness, and with blindness, and with astonishment of heart;

11492.text: and you shall grope at noonday, as the blind gropes in darkness, and you shall not prosper in your ways: and you shall be only oppressed and robbed always, and there shall be none to save you.

11493.text: You shall betroth a wife, and another man shall lie with her: you shall build a house, and you shall not dwell therein: you shall plant a vineyard, and shall not use its fruit.

11494.text: Your ox shall be slain before your eyes, and you shall not eat of it: your donkey shall be violently taken away from before your face, and shall not be restored to you: your sheep shall be given to your enemies, and you shall have none to save you.

11495.text: Your sons and your daughters shall be given to another people; and your eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day: and there shall be nothing in the power of your hand.

11496.text: The fruit of your ground, and all your labors, shall a nation which you do not know eat up; and you shall be only oppressed and crushed always;

11497.text: so that you shall be mad for the sight of your eyes which you shall see.

11498.text: The Lord will strike you in the knees, and in the legs, with a sore boil, of which you can not be healed, from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head.

11499.text: The Lord will bring you, and your king whom you shall set over you, to a nation that you have not known, you nor your fathers; and there you shall serve other gods, wood and stone.

11500.text: You shall become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all the peoples where the Lord shall lead you away.

11501.text: You shall carry much seed out into the field, and shall gather little in; for the locust shall consume it.

11502.text: You shall plant vineyards and dress them, but you shall neither drink of the wine, nor harvest; for the worm shall eat them.

11503.text: You shall have olive trees throughout all your borders, but you shall not anoint yourself with the oil; for your olives shall drop off.

11504.text: You shall father sons and daughters, but they shall not be yours; for they shall go into captivity.

11505.text: All your trees and the fruit of your ground shall the locust possess.

11506.text: The foreigner who is in the midst of you shall mount up above you higher and higher; and you shall come down lower and lower.

11507.text: He shall lend to you, and you shall not lend to him: he shall be the head, and you shall be the tail.

11508.text: All these curses shall come on you, and shall pursue you, and overtake you, until you are destroyed; because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord your God, to keep his commandments and his statutes which he commanded you:

11509.text: and they shall be on you for a sign and for a wonder, and on your seed forever.

11510.text: Because you did not serve the Lord your God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, by reason of the abundance of all things;

11511.text: therefore you shall serve your enemies whom the Lord shall send against you, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things: and he shall put a yoke of iron on your neck, until he has destroyed you.

11512.text: The Lord will bring a nation against you from far, from the end of the earth, as the eagle flies; a nation whose language you shall not understand;

11513.text: a nation of fierce facial expressions, that shall not respect the person of the old, nor show favor to the young,

11514.text: and shall eat the fruit of your livestock, and the fruit of your ground, until you are destroyed; that also shall not leave you grain, new wine, or oil, the increase of your livestock, or the young of your flock, until they have caused you to perish.

11515.text: They shall besiege you in all your gates, until your high and fortified walls come down, in which you trusted, throughout all your land; and they shall besiege you in all your gates throughout all your land, which the Lord your God has given you.

11516.text: You shall eat the fruit of your own body, the flesh of your sons and of your daughters, whom the Lord your God has given you, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemies shall distress you.

11517.text: The man who is tender among you, and very delicate, his eye shall be evil toward his brother, and toward the wife of his bosom, and toward the remnant of his children whom he has remaining;

11518.text: so that he will not give to any of them of the flesh of his children whom he shall eat, because he has nothing left him, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy shall distress you in all your gates.

11519.text: The tender and delicate woman among you, who would not adventure to set the sole of her foot on the ground for delicateness and tenderness, her eye shall be evil toward the husband of her bosom, and toward her son, and toward her daughter,

11520.text: and toward her young one who comes out from between her feet, and toward her children whom she shall bear; for she shall eat them for want of all things secretly, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy shall distress you in your gates.

11521.text: If you will not observe to do all the words of this law that are written in this book, that you may fear this glorious and fearful name, The Lord your God;

11522.text: then the Lord will make your plagues wonderful, and the plagues of your seed, even great plagues, and of long continuance, and severe sicknesses, and of long continuance.

11523.text: He will bring on you again all the diseases of Egypt, which you were afraid of; and they shall cling to you.

11524.text: Also every sickness, and every plague, which is not written in the book of this law, the Lord will bring them on you, until you are destroyed.

11525.text: You shall be left few in number, whereas you were as the stars of the sky for multitude; because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord your God.

11526.text: It shall happen that as the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good, and to multiply you, so the Lord will rejoice over you to cause you to perish, and to destroy you; and you shall be plucked from off the land where you go in to possess it.

11527.text: The Lord will scatter you among all peoples, from the one end of the earth even to the other end of the earth; and there you shall serve other gods, which you have not known, you nor your fathers, even wood and stone.

11528.text: Among these nations you shall find no ease, and there shall be no rest for the sole of your foot: but the Lord will give you there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and pining of soul;

11529.text: and your life shall hang in doubt before you; and you shall fear night and day, and shall have no assurance of your life.

11530.text: In the morning you shall say, "I wish it were evening!" and at evening you shall say, "I wish it were morning!" for the fear of your heart which you shall fear, and for the sight of your eyes which you shall see.

11531.text: The Lord will bring you into Egypt again with ships, by the way of which I said to you, You shall see it no more again: and there you shall sell yourselves to your enemies for bondservants and for bondmaids, and no man shall buy you.

11532.text: These are the words of the covenant which the Lord commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant which he made with them in Horeb.

11533.text: Moses called to all Israel, and said to them, You have seen all that the Lord did before your eyes in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land;

11534.text: the great trials which your eyes saw, the signs, and those great wonders:

11535.text: but the Lord has not given you a heart to know, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, to this day.

11536.text: I have led you forty years in the wilderness: your clothes have not grown old on you, and your shoes have not grown old on your feet.

11537.text: You have not eaten bread, neither have you drunk wine or strong drink; that you may know that I am the Lord your God.

11538.text: When you came to this place, Sihon the king of Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan, came out against us to battle, and we struck them:

11539.text: and we took their land, and gave it for an inheritance to the Reubenites, and to the Gadites, and to the half-tribe of the Manassites.

11540.text: Keep therefore the words of this covenant, and do them, that you may prosper in all that you do.

11541.text: You stand this day all of you before the Lord your God; your heads, your tribes, your elders, and your officers, even all the men of Israel,

11542.text: your little ones, your wives, and your foreigner who is in the midst of your camps, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water;

11543.text: that you may enter into the covenant of the Lord your God, and into his oath, which the Lord your God makes with you this day;

11544.text: that he may establish you this day to himself for a people, and that he may be to you a God, as he spoke to you, and as he swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

11545.text: Neither with you only do I make this covenant and this oath,

11546.text: but with him who stands here with us this day before the Lord our God, and also with him who is not here with us this day

11547.text: (for you know how we lived in the land of Egypt, and how we came through the midst of the nations through which you passed;

11548.text: and you have seen their abominations, and their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, which were among them);

11549.text: lest there should be among you man, or woman, or family, or tribe, whose heart turns away this day from the Lord our God, to go to serve the gods of those nations; lest there should be among you a root that bears gall and wormwood;

11550.text: and it happen, when he hears the words of this curse, that he bless himself in his heart, saying, "I shall have peace, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart, to destroy the moist with the dry."

11551.text: The Lord will not pardon him, but then the anger of the Lord and his jealousy will smoke against that man, and all the curse that is written in this book shall lie on him, and the Lord will blot out his name from under the sky.

11552.text: The Lord will set him apart to evil out of all the tribes of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant that is written in this book of the law.

11553.text: The generation to come, your children who shall rise up after you, and the foreigner who shall come from a far land, shall say, when they see the plagues of that land, and the sicknesses with which the Lord has made it sick;

11554.text: and that the whole land of it is sulfur, salt, and burning, that it is not sown, nor bears, nor any grass grows therein, like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the Lord overthrew in his anger, and in his wrath:

11555.text: even all the nations shall say, "Why has the Lord done thus to this land? What does the heat of this great anger mean?"

11556.text: Then men shall say, "Because they forsook the covenant of the Lord, the God of their fathers, which he made with them when he brought them forth out of the land of Egypt,

11557.text: and went and served other gods, and worshiped them, gods that they did not know, and that he had not given to them:

11558.text: therefore the anger of the Lord was kindled against this land, to bring on it all the curse that is written in this book;

11559.text: and the Lord rooted them out of their land in anger, and in wrath, and in great indignation, and cast them into another land, as at this day."

11560.text: The secret things belong to the Lord our God; but the things that are revealed belong to us and to our children forever, that we may do all the words of this law.

11561.text: It shall happen, when all these things have come on you, the blessing and the curse, which I have set before you, and you shall call them to mind among all the nations, where the Lord your God has driven you,

11562.text: and shall return to the Lord your God, and shall obey his voice according to all that I command you this day, you and your children, with all your heart, and with all your soul;

11563.text: that then the Lord your God will turn your captivity, and have compassion on you, and will return and gather you from all the peoples, where the Lord your God has scattered you.

11564.text: If your outcasts are in the uttermost parts of the heavens, from there will the Lord your God gather you, and from there he will bring you back:

11565.text: and the Lord your God will bring you into the land which your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it; and he will do you good, and multiply you above your fathers.

11566.text: The Lord your God will circumcise your heart, and the heart of your seed, to love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, that you may live.

11567.text: The Lord your God will put all these curses on your enemies, and on those who hate you, who persecuted you.

11568.text: You shall return and obey the voice of the Lord, and do all his commandments which I command you this day.

11569.text: The Lord your God will make you plenteous in all the work of your hand, in the fruit of your body, and in the fruit of your ground, and in the fruit of your livestock, for the Lord will again rejoice over you for good, as he rejoiced over your fathers;

11570.text: if you shall obey the voice of the Lord your God, to keep his commandments and his statutes which are written in this book of the law; if you turn to the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul.

11571.text: For this commandment which I command you this day, it is not too hard for you, neither is it far off.

11572.text: It is not in heaven, that you should say, "Who shall go up for us to heaven, and bring it to us, and make us to hear it, that we may do it?"

11573.text: Neither is it beyond the sea, that you should say, "Who shall go over the sea for us, and bring it to us, and make us to hear it, that we may do it?"

11574.text: But the word is very near to you, in your mouth, and in your heart, that you may do it.

11575.text: Behold, I have set before you this day life and good, and death and evil;

11576.text: in that I command you this day to love the Lord your God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his ordinances, that you may live and multiply, and that the Lord your God may bless you in the land where you go in to possess it.

11577.text: But if your heart turns away, and you will not hear, but shall be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them;

11578.text: I denounce to you this day, that you shall surely perish; you shall not prolong your days in the land, where you pass over the Jordan to go in to possess it.

11579.text: I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse: therefore choose life, that you may live, you and your seed;

11580.text: to love the Lord your God, to obey his voice, and to cling to him; for he is your life, and the length of your days; that you may dwell in the land which the Lord swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.

11581.text: Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.

11582.text: He said to them, "I am one hundred twenty years old this day; I can no more go out and come in: and the Lord has said to me, 'You shall not go over this Jordan.'

11583.text: The Lord your God, he will go over before you; he will destroy these nations from before you, and you shall dispossess them. Joshua shall go over before you, as the Lord has spoken.

11584.text: The Lord will do to them as he did to Sihon and to Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land; whom he destroyed.

11585.text: The Lord will deliver them up before you, and you shall do to them according to all the commandment which I have commanded you.

11586.text: Be strong and courageous, do not be afraid, nor be scared of them: for the Lord your God, he it is who does go with you; he will not fail you, nor forsake you."

11587.text: Moses called to Joshua, and said to him in the sight of all Israel, "Be strong and courageous: for you shall go with this people into the land which the Lord has sworn to their fathers to give them; and you shall cause them to inherit it.

11588.text: The Lord, he it is who does go before you; he will be with you, he will not fail you, neither forsake you: do not be afraid, neither be dismayed."

11589.text: Moses wrote this law, and delivered it to the priests the sons of Levi, who bore the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and to all the elders of Israel.

11590.text: Moses commanded them, saying, "At the end of every seven years, in the set time of the year of release, in the feast of tents,

11591.text: when all Israel has come to appear before the Lord your God in the place which he shall choose, you shall read this law before all Israel in their hearing.

11592.text: Assemble the people, the men and the women and the little ones, and your foreigner who is within your gates, that they may hear, and that they may learn, and fear the Lord your God, and observe to do all the words of this law;

11593.text: and that their children, who have not known, may hear, and learn to fear the Lord your God, as long as you live in the land where you go over the Jordan to possess it."

11594.text: The Lord said to Moses, "Behold, your days approach that you must die: call Joshua, and present yourselves in the Tent of Meeting, that I may commission him." Moses and Joshua went, and presented themselves in the Tent of Meeting.

11595.text: The Lord appeared in the Tent in a pillar of cloud: and the pillar of cloud stood over the door of the Tent.

11596.text: The Lord said to Moses, "Behold, you shall sleep with your fathers; and this people will rise up, and play the prostitute after the strange gods of the land, where they go to be among them, and will forsake me, and break my covenant which I have made with them.

11597.text: Then my anger shall be kindled against them in that day, and I will forsake them, and I will hide my face from them, and they shall be devoured, and many evils and troubles shall come on them; so that they will say in that day, 'Haven't these evils come on us because our God is not among us?'

11598.text: I will surely hide my face in that day for all the evil which they shall have worked, in that they are turned to other gods.

11599.text: "Now therefore write this song for yourselves, and teach it to the children of Israel: put it in their mouths, that this song may be a witness for me against the children of Israel.

11600.text: For when I shall have brought them into the land which I swore to their fathers, flowing with milk and honey, and they shall have eaten and filled themselves, and grown fat; then will they turn to other gods, and serve them, and despise me, and break my covenant.

11601.text: It shall happen, when many evils and troubles have come on them, that this song shall testify before them as a witness; for it shall not be forgotten out of the mouths of their seed: for I know their imagination which they frame this day, before I have brought them into the land which I swore."

11602.text: So Moses wrote this song the same day, and taught it the children of Israel.

11603.text: He commissioned Joshua the son of Nun, and said, "Be strong and courageous; for you shall bring the children of Israel into the land which I swore to them: and I will be with you."

11604.text: It happened, when Moses had made an end of writing the words of this law in a book, until they were finished,

11605.text: that Moses commanded the Levites, who bore the ark of the covenant of the Lord, saying,

11606.text: "Take this book of the law, and put it by the side of the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, that it may be there for a witness against you.

11607.text: For I know your rebellion, and your stiff neck: behold, while I am yet alive with you this day, you have been rebellious against the Lord; and how much more after my death?

11608.text: Assemble to me all the elders of your tribes, and your officers, that I may speak these words in their ears, and call heaven and earth to witness against them.

11609.text: For I know that after my death you will utterly corrupt yourselves, and turn aside from the way which I have commanded you; and evil will happen to you in the latter days; because you will do that which is evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger through the work of your hands."

11610.text: Moses spoke in the ears of all the assembly of Israel the words of this song, until they were finished.

11611.text: Give ear, you heavens, and I will speak. Let the earth hear the words of my mouth.

11612.text: My doctrine shall drop as the rain. My speech shall condense as the dew, as the small rain on the tender grass, as the showers on the herb.

11613.text: For I will proclaim the name of the Lord. Ascribe greatness to our God!

11614.text: The Rock, his work is perfect, for all his ways are justice: a God of faithfulness and without iniquity, just and right is he.

11615.text: They have dealt corruptly with him. They are not his children, because of their defect. They are a perverse and crooked generation.

11616.text: Do you thus requite the Lord, foolish people and unwise? Isn't he your father who has bought you? He has made you, and established you.

11617.text: Remember the days of old. Consider the years of many generations. Ask your father, and he will show you; your elders, and they will tell you.

11618.text: When the Most High gave to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the children of men, he set the bounds of the peoples according to the number of the children of Israel.

11619.text: For the Lord's portion is his people. Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.

11620.text: He found him in a desert land, in the waste howling wilderness. He surrounded him. He cared for him. He kept him as the apple of his eye.

11621.text: As an eagle that stirs up her nest, that flutters over her young, he spread abroad his wings, he took them, he bore them on his feathers.

11622.text: The Lord alone led him. There was no foreign god with him.

11623.text: He made him ride on the high places of the earth. He ate the increase of the field. He caused him to suck honey out of the rock, oil out of the flinty rock;

11624.text: Butter of the herd, and milk of the flock, with fat of lambs, rams of the breed of Bashan, and goats, with the finest of the wheat. Of the blood of the grape you drank wine.

11625.text: But Jeshurun grew fat, and kicked. You have grown fat. You have grown thick. You have become sleek. Then he forsook God who made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation.

11626.text: They moved him to jealousy with strange gods. They provoked him to anger with abominations.

11627.text: They sacrificed to demons, not God, to gods that they did not know, to new gods that came up recently, which your fathers did not dread.

11628.text: Of the Rock who became your father, you are unmindful, and have forgotten God who gave you birth.

11629.text: The Lord saw and abhorred, because of the provocation of his sons and his daughters.

11630.text: He said, "I will hide my face from them. I will see what their end shall be; for they are a very perverse generation, children in whom is no faithfulness.

11631.text: They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God. They have provoked me to anger with their vanities. I will move them to jealousy with those who are not a people. I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.

11632.text: For a fire is kindled in my anger, Burns to the lowest Sheol, Devours the earth with its increase, and sets the foundations of the mountains on fire.

11633.text: "I will heap evils on them. I will spend my arrows on them.

11634.text: They shall be wasted with hunger, and devoured with burning heat and bitter destruction. I will send the teeth of animals on them, With the poison of crawling things of the dust.

11635.text: Outside the sword shall bereave, and in the rooms, terror; on both young man and virgin, The nursing infant with the gray-haired man.

11636.text: I said, I would scatter them afar. I would make their memory to cease from among men;

11637.text: were it not that I feared the provocation of the enemy, lest their adversaries should judge wrongly, lest they should say, 'Our hand is exalted, the Lord has not done all this.'"

11638.text: For they are a nation void of counsel. There is no understanding in them.

11639.text: Oh that they were wise, that they understood this, that they would consider their latter end!

11640.text: How could one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them, and the Lord had delivered them up?

11641.text: For their rock is not as our Rock, even our enemies themselves being judges.

11642.text: For their vine is of the vine of Sodom, of the fields of Gomorrah. Their grapes are grapes of gall, Their clusters are bitter.

11643.text: Their wine is the poison of serpents, The cruel venom of asps.

11644.text: "Isn't this laid up in store with me, sealed up among my treasures?

11645.text: Vengeance is mine, and I will repay, at the time when their foot slides; for the day of their calamity is at hand. The things that are to come on them shall make haste."

11646.text: For the Lord will judge his people, and have compassion on his servants, when he sees that their power is gone, There is none remaining, shut up or left at large.

11647.text: He will say, "Where are their gods, The rock in which they took refuge;

11648.text: Which ate the fat of their sacrifices, And drank the wine of their drink offering? Let them rise up and help you! Let them be your protection.

11649.text: "See now that I, even I, am he, There is no god with me. I kill, and I make alive. I wound, and I heal. There is no one who can deliver out of my hand.

11650.text: For I lift up my hand to heaven, And say, As I live forever,

11651.text: if I whet my glittering sword, My hand take hold on judgment; I will render vengeance to my adversaries, and will recompense those who hate me.

11652.text: I will make my arrows drunk with blood. My sword shall devour flesh with the blood of the slain and the captives, from the head of the leaders of the enemy."

11653.text: Rejoice, O heavens, with him, and let all the angels of God worship him. Rejoice, O nations, with his people, and let all the angels of God strengthen themselves in him. For he will avenge the blood of his sons, and render vengeance to his enemies, and will recompense them that hate him, and will cleanse the land for his people.

11654.text: Moses came and spoke all the words of this song in the ears of the people, he and Joshua the son of Nun.

11655.text: Moses made an end of speaking all these words to all Israel;

11656.text: He said to them, "Set your heart to all the words which I testify to you this day, which you shall command your children to observe to do, all the words of this law.

11657.text: For it is no vain thing for you; because it is your life, and through this thing you shall prolong your days in the land, where you go over the Jordan to possess it."

11658.text: The Lord spoke to Moses that same day, saying,

11659.text: "Go up into this mountain of Abarim, to Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab, that is over against Jericho; and see the land of Canaan, which I give to the children of Israel for a possession;

11660.text: and die on the mountain where you go up, and be gathered to your people, as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor, and was gathered to his people:

11661.text: because you trespassed against me in the midst of the children of Israel at the waters of Meribah of Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin; because you did not sanctify me in the midst of the children of Israel.

11662.text: For you shall see the land before you; but you shall not go there into the land which I give the children of Israel."

11663.text: This is the blessing, with which Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel before his death.

11664.text: He said, "The Lord came from Sinai, And rose from Seir to them. He shone forth from Mount Paran. He came from the ten thousands of holy ones. At his right hand was a fiery law for them.

11665.text: Yes, he loves the people. All his saints are in your hand. They sat down at your feet; each receives your words.

11666.text: Moses commanded us a law, An inheritance for the assembly of Jacob.

11667.text: He was king in Jeshurun, When the heads of the people were gathered, All the tribes of Israel together.

11668.text: "Let Reuben live, and not die; Nor let his men be few."

11669.text: This is for Judah. He said, "Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah. Bring him in to his people. With his hands he contended for himself. You shall be a help against his adversaries."

11670.text: Of Levi he said, "Your Thummim and your Urim are with your godly one, whom you proved at Massah, with whom you strove at the waters of Meribah;

11671.text: who said of his father, and of his mother, 'I have not seen him;' Neither did he acknowledge his brothers, Nor did he know his own children: For they have observed your word, and keep your covenant.

11672.text: They shall teach Jacob your ordinances, and Israel your law. They shall put incense before you, and whole burnt offering on your altar.

11673.text: The Lord, bless his substance. Accept the work of his hands. Strike through the hips of those who rise up against him, of those who hate him, that they not rise again."

11674.text: Of Benjamin he said, "The beloved of the Lord shall dwell in safety by him. He covers him all the day long. He dwells between his shoulders."

11675.text: Of Joseph he said, "His land is blessed by the Lord, for the precious things of the heavens, for the dew, for the deep that couches beneath,

11676.text: for the precious things of the fruits of the sun, for the precious things of the growth of the moons,

11677.text: for the chief things of the ancient mountains, for the precious things of the everlasting hills,

11678.text: for the precious things of the earth and its fullness, the good will of him who lived in the bush. Let this come on the head of Joseph, on the crown of the head of him who was separate from his brothers.

11679.text: The firstborn of his herd, majesty is his. His horns are the horns of the wild ox. With them he shall push all of the peoples, to the ends of the earth: They are the ten thousands of Ephraim. They are the thousands of Manasseh."

11680.text: Of Zebulun he said, "Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out; and Issachar, in your tents.

11681.text: They shall call the peoples to the mountain. There they will offer sacrifices of righteousness, for they shall draw out the abundance of the seas, the hidden treasures of the sand."

11682.text: Of Gad he said, "He who enlarges Gad is blessed. He dwells as a lioness, and tears the arm, yes, the crown of the head.

11683.text: He provided the first part for himself, for there was the lawgiver's portion reserved. He came with the heads of the people. He executed the righteousness of the Lord, His ordinances with Israel."

11684.text: Of Dan he said, "Dan is a lion's cub that leaps out of Bashan."

11685.text: Of Naphtali he said, "Naphtali, satisfied with favor, full of the blessing of the Lord, Possess the west and the south."

11686.text: Of Asher he said, "Asher is blessed with children. Let him be acceptable to his brothers. Let him dip his foot in oil.

11687.text: Your bars shall be iron and brass. As your days, so your strength will be.

11688.text: "There is none like God, Jeshurun, who rides on the heavens for your help, In his majesty through the skies.

11689.text: The eternal God is your dwelling place. Underneath are the everlasting arms. He thrust out the enemy from before you, and said, 'Destroy!'

11690.text: Israel dwells in safety; the fountain of Jacob alone, In a land of grain and new wine. Yes, his heavens drop down dew.

11691.text: You are happy, Israel. Who is like you, a people saved by the Lord, the shield of your help, the sword of your excellency! Your enemies shall submit themselves to you. You shall tread on their high places."

11692.text: Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is over against Jericho. The Lord showed him all the land of Gilead, to Dan,

11693.text: and all Naphtali, and the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah, to the hinder sea,

11694.text: and the Negev, and the Plain of the valley of Jericho the city of palm trees, to Zoar.

11695.text: The Lord said to him, "This is the land which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, 'I will give it to your seed.' I have caused you to see it with your eyes, but you shall not go over there."

11696.text: So Moses the servant of the Lord died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the Lord.

11697.text: And he buried him in the valley in the land of Moab over against Beth Peor: but no man knows of his tomb to this day.

11698.text: Moses was one hundred twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.

11699.text: The children of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days: so the days of weeping in the mourning for Moses were ended.

11700.text: Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands on him: and the children of Israel listened to him, and did as the Lord commanded Moses.

11701.text: There has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face,

11702.text: in all the signs and the wonders, which the Lord sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land,

11703.text: and in all the mighty hand, and in all the great terror, which Moses worked in the sight of all Israel.
